findings.quote: regarding nothing as belonging to others and everything as theirs to plunder
findings.problem: Greek: οὐδὲν οἰκεῖον, πάντα δ᾽ ἡγούμενοι πολέμια. οἰκεῖον means 'friendly/kindred', opposed to πολέμια 'hostile': they regard nothing as friendly and everything as hostile. The English inverts/misreads the antithesis.
findings.proposed_fix: regarding nothing as friendly and everything as hostile

units.note: The phrase τῶν ἐξηρμένων τὸν ἄνδρα κατὰ πάντα τρόπον is obscure; the English is an acceptable rendering and left alone.

findings.quote: he had in effect handed over the whole of his command to Dorimachus
findings.problem: Greek: παρακεχωρήκει τούτῳ τῆς ὅλης ἀρχῆς, after 'Δωριμάχου καὶ Σκόπα'. τούτῳ is singular and its antecedent is ambiguous; the nearest name is Scopas, and Scopas is the one who leads the action that follows. The English silently resolves it to Dorimachus. The singular may be a corruption of τούτοις (both).
findings.proposed_fix: he had in effect handed over the whole of his command to the latter

units.note: Genuinely ambiguous or possibly corrupt (τούτῳ vs τούτοις); 'the latter' keeps the Greek's own ambiguity. Numbers checked: Philip aged 17 (ἑπτακαίδεκα) is correct.
